name: SDXL + LoRA Image
description: Text-to-image with an SDXL checkpoint plus a character/style LoRA — a consistent trained identity or style rendered from a prompt.

prompt.description: Comma-separated tags and short phrases, not a sentence — same tag syntax as sdxl_base: subject first, atmosphere last, `(term:1.2)` to weight a term, roughly 75 tokens of content before the tail stops pulling. What differs here is the LoRA. Most character and style LoRAs fire on a trigger word, and without it in the prompt the LoRA loads and does close to nothing: put the trigger at the front, then describe only what the LoRA does not already carry — pose, clothing, setting, light. Describing the face a character LoRA was trained on fights it. The LoRA's model page is where the trigger word is stated; there is no way to read it off the file.

negative_prompt.description: What to steer away from, same tag syntax. Keep it to defects you actually see — 'blurry, low quality, extra fingers, watermark'. An oversized negative eats guidance and flattens the image.

examples.prompt: <lora trigger word>, seated at a café table, morning light through the window, denim jacket, medium shot, photorealistic
examples.negative_prompt: blurry, low quality, extra fingers, watermark
